articles.summary: HBO HBO's Harry Potter TV series will be the Christmas present that the entire world gets this year, and hopefully it's one they want to keep. The series will offer a long-form version of what a generation of fans got from the Harry Potter films, and (hopefully) will take readers of the books on a much […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google HBO's Harry Potter TV series will be the Christmas present that the entire world gets this year, and hopefully it's one they want to keep. The series will offer a long-form version of what a generation of fans got from the Harry Potter films, and (hopefully) will take readers of the books on a much more complete and familiar journey. As the premiere date gets closer, we're seeing much more of what the finished production looks like, and diehard fans are spotting some pretty fine details that show the level of fidelity the show is showing to the text.

The latest set of Harry Potter promotional images showcases a milestone moment from the first novel, Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone : Harry Potter's first trip to Diagon Alley, the hidden magical market where all Wizards and Witches go to shop for their mystic essentials. However, fans are also taking note of something else in the image: the fashion Harry is wearing before he gets some proper wizard's robes.

The official Harry Potter website posted a new featured article titled "Six fashionable findings from the HBO Original Harry Potter series costume department". It helps viewers get a deeper sense of the intense level of detail that was put into the show. The first item on the list is "How to spot magical people in the Muggle world," and it features the above image of Harry Potter (actor Dominic McLaughlin) taking in the wonder of Diagon Alley, while wearing an outfit that very much looks like what a '90s kid would be wearing.

In the breakdown, the style and design team behind Harry Potter describe how they had to create a sense of fashion for the Wizarding World that felt like it could plausibly exist alongside the fashion of non-magic humans (or "Muggles") of the time. That meant "a lot of synthetics. The costume department scoured charity shops and rag-and-bone yards, consulting their family albums for unglamourous ensembles to represent early 90s fashion: unfiltered."

There's also an interesting amount of logic that went into guiding the style choices for the series: "Magical people don’t stick to trends," the site states. "They would likely ditch high street shops for jumble sales, culminating in more eclectic, unconventional wardrobes. Don’t expect all witches and wizards to look the same."

There's an even deeper dive into the fashion of Harry Potter (2026), check it out on the franchise's official site .

The Harry Potter movies that Warner Bros. put out started in 2001 with Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone , and ended in 2011 with Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2 . The studio chose to update the story to a modern-day setting (at that time), meaning that characters wore 2000s fashion trends to make them relatable to audience members of similar age. It raised some ire with hardcore fans of the books, as there are some deeper metaphors and symbolism about real-world politics and culture at that time, which were invariably altered by the time shift.

Now, the TV series is going the opposite route with its period piece format. It'll be interesting to see how viewers react to that, and if the book-accurate setting really does change or enhance the experience of the story, in visual form.

Harry Potter will premiere on HBO on Christmas Day. Do you like the '90s look?

articles.title: Charles Barkley Pitched His Potential Inside The NBA Replacement, But I Have Another Idea
articles.summary: This isn't a bad pick, but another host is on my mind.
articles.content:
As Inside the NBA ’s latest season on ESPN continues, questions continue to swirl around the show in regard to its future. Longtime co-host Ernie Johnson has officially confirmed his plans to leave the show at the end of this season, and colleague Charles Barkley apparently plans to do the same. There’s been a lot of discussion regarding who might replace the beloved sports commentators, and Barkley recently pitched his successor. While it’s a solid pick, I’d admittedly prefer to see another seasoned pundit take over Barkley’s post.

Barkley – also known as “The Round Mound of Rebound” to some – is definitely someone who loves to speak his mind. So it doesn’t surprise me at all that he’d have thoughts on who might be able to take his place on Inside . The former Phoenix Sun was recently quoted as saying he didn’t believe anyone but fellow ex-player Jalen Rose could replace him at the desk. That comment was brought up to Rose when he was interviewed by Front Office Sports (as seen on YouTube ) and, when asked about the job, he said this:

The notion of Rose taking over for Barkley is actually quite reasonable, considering his resume as a broadcaster. He’s not only served as a fill-in analyst for Inside the NBA for years now, but he’s also taken on hosting duties for ABC/ESPN over the years. I personally enjoy seeing Rose when he appears on Inside , and his relaxed demeanor usually serves as a firm counterbalance to others on the dais like the vivacious Barkley or Shaquille O’Neal . With that said, there’s another recurring analyst I’d love to see join the show instead.

Inside has welcomed plenty of insightful and entertaining guest hosts over the years, from the cool Vince Carter to the wise-cracking Draymond Green (who has a rivalry with Charles Barkley) . Someone who, for me, has always been a welcome presence on the show is Chris Webber, who’s been appearing on the show for years. He obviously has plenty of broadcasting experience, and he’s a wealth of knowledge when it comes to basketball. I’d say the show would be lucky to have him full-time.

Again, though, this isn’t to say that Jalen Rose wouldn’t be able to do the job effectively. There may actually be a reality in which both players end up on the show full time by next season. However, that’s assuming ESPN is looking to bring on two former players and not get another non-ex-player analyst to specifically fill the void that’ll be left by Johnson.

To be honest, it may also behoove me not to get too ahead of myself right now, as the season is still young. Also, while Charles Barkley’s retirement claim is seeming more likely , he hasn’t said much more about it in the wake of Ernie Johnson’s announcement. We’ll just have to wait and see what happens and how the producers choose to proceed should Barkley leave the fold along with Johnson.

articles.title: Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving Special Isn't Good, But There Are 5 Reasons To Still Watch it

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving from 1973 is arguably among the least thrilling of the Peanuts' animated antics, especially from the retro era of the cartoon. Even Charlie Brown himself seems tired of his holiday specials, remorsefully lamenting to Linus, "We've got another holiday to worry about." While I agree with his sister Sally's complaints about how she has barely finished her Halloween candy, this cartoon offers very few memorable gags and seems more contrived than it does original. What it lacks in standing out among its dozens of peers , it makes up for it in a few ways that shockingly make it worth the watch.

Charlie Brown is off to visit his Grandmother to celebrate with his family, but his plans are interrupted by Peppermint Patty when she invites herself over to his home to spend the holiday. He finds himself in an even worse predicament when his guest list grows from one classmate to many more, and he's forced to figure out how to entertain and feed an entire cavalcade of kids. As if the general feeling of existential dread and anxiety that Charlie Brown walks around with on a daily basis wasn't enough, now he has to figure out how to roast a turkey when all he knows how to do is burn toast and pour milk on cereal. It sounds straightforward, and it is — but the road to that festive meal includes a handful of elements that make this Thanksgiving cartoon something to add in your holiday viewing rotation.

Peppermint Patty is an iconic part of the Peanuts cast, but she wasn't an original one when the strip debuted back in 1950 (although there was someone named Patty but these two characters are not the same). It wasn't until Aug. 1966 that the green-shirted brunette first stepped her sandals onto newspaper strips. This was the same year that It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown! first hit the airwaves on CBS, but there would be six more animated specials in between this Thanksgiving toon before we finally saw her in an animated format.

A friend of "Chuck's" as she prefers to call him, Peppermint Patty inserted herself into Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving plans rather abruptly, but in her mind she was entitled to his attention. Throughout her time in the series, Patty has shown an interest in the yellow-shirted blockhead that goes beyond friendship. She's very forward with him on the phone, leaving him blushing and at a loss for words. While it isn't shown in this special, Patty's companion Marcie also has a crush on the same guy — something he has zero ability to handle. Charlie Brown is not much for romance and is the furthest thing from a casanova, so it's funny to watch him in these situations where he probably enjoys the attention from a girl but has no idea what to do with it.

Vince Guaraldi had been working with Charles Schulz and the Peanuts gang as far back as 1963, predating the first animated Christmas special. Alongside his trio and later quintet, Guaraldi composed and played his jazz stylings through a dozen Charlie Brown cartoons, with this one among the group. If the Christmas soundtrack was more melancholy and the Halloween special a bit more serious and spooky, the Thanksgiving special is more upbeat and light-hearted to match the nature of its story.

Guaraldi's updated reprise of "Linus and Lucy" for Snoopy's cooking montage is a jam that keeps on giving, adding more flair to one of his most well-known jazz compositions that has become the theme song for the franchise. Where the soundtrack shines the most is "Little Birdie," a song that introduces Woodstock into the mix during this toon. The majority of Guaraldi's work on the series were instrumental, but "Little Birdie" is one of the few songs across the series that has lyrics, but one of a very tiny selection that the artist sang by himself. His expressive and soulful voice backed by sounds of brass and bass is extremely catchy and will stick with you long after the memory of the cartoon disappears.

There are some pretty solid visual gags throughout the Thanksgiving show, including one of my favorite sequences with Snoopy brawling against a lawn chair in a clash of champions that is not as one-sided as you might think. But throughout the entire show, it's Woodstock who steals the show as the funniest element that keeps the audience laughing and wondering what he will do next. It's impossible not to love the tiny yellow bird, and he adds a ton of comedy relief alongside Snoopy. Their relationship is often more Laurel & Hardy, with Snoopy using his size to make some jokes about their power dynamic, but Woodstock always shines and makes sure both buddies come out on top.

Besides helping Snoopy cook the non-traditional Thanksgiving meal (more on that in a second), Woodstock joined his pal in dressing up as pilgrims in a very silly segment that involves a luggage trunk and some oversized hats. If Snoopy and Woodstock came from overseas to colonize my people, I'd be a little less apprehensive about it than a ship full of British people. Woodstock simply makes everything better, and he was another great addition to the Peanuts roster that brought a ton of energy to this otherwise bland affair.

Since Charlie Brown is catering a meal for kids who aren't allowed to use a stove without parental guidance, he does the rational thing and employs his dog and bird friend to do all the cooking. Snoopy puts on his adorable chefs hat and gets to work, making popcorn and buttered toast to accompany their side dishes of jellybeans and pretzel sticks. If you were a child making dinner who had no idea how to cook, this is basically what you would do. Anyone can operate a toaster, even a canine who may or may not have opposable thumbs.

Snoopy would make Martha Stewart proud, decorating a ping-pong table with a lovely linen cloth and origami-folded napkins. While it's all very nice, what upsets me is Snoopy's lack of beverages for the kids. Mysterious pink sundae cups appear on the table during the feast with no explanation (and we're never shown who made them or what they actually are), so we can assume whatever cherry-topped concoction in there is in place of their drinks. If I was eating all that salt, dry bread and tooth-decaying snacks, I'd want something to sip on, but we can only expect so much. After all, Snoopy needed time to work on his pilgrim costume with Woodstock. He has his priorities, but we appreciate him making the time and putting in the effort to feed this makeshift group.

Peppermint Patty might think Charlie Brown is cute, but her patience for his spontaneous Thanksgiving party is practically non-existent. Besides inviting herself over without asking, Patty rudely complains to the entire party about the meal and berates him in front of the guests. It isn't until Marcie reminds her compatriot that she was never actually asked to come, and may have hurt his feelings with her brusque words. Charlie Brown takes it to heart and worries he ruined Thanksgiving for everyone, but Marcie reminds him that they should all be thankful to be together while Patty apologizes for playing "lover's games" and the group reconcile.

In the end, all of the kids are invited to Charlie Brown's grandmother's condo to celebrate Thanksgiving. Meanwhile, Snoopy and Woodstock stay home and enjoy a secret traditional meal with the yellow bird eating one of his distant cousins with a smile. That might be the most memorable thing about this special, but I'm choosing to ignore that one because I don't want to have Charlie Brown levels of anxiety thinking about Woodstock as a cannibal. But what should stay with you more is how the ultimate message in this cartoon was a very practical lesson in gratitude. The main course is "Be happy with what you have and not what you don't" with a side of "friends are family," differentiating it from other Thanksgiving specials that focus on just the general idea of being thankful. It's a bit more nuanced and surprisingly mature for a kids cartoon, but we shouldn't expect less from a boy named Charlie Brown.

Do you have any memories of the Charlie Brown Thanksgiving special, or maybe a different nostalgic cartoon about Turkey Day? Join the conversation and let us know in the comments below.

articles.summary: Bungie has created one of its best cinematic trailers yet for Marathon's newest Shell, Bishop, which is saying a lot considering how great the studio is at these. Each Shell trailer showcases the character, but this is easily one of the most impressive and stylish. In it, Bungie reveals Bishop, a striking new Shell that […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Bungie has created one of its best cinematic trailers yet for Marathon's newest Shell, Bishop, which is saying a lot considering how great the studio is at these. Each Shell trailer showcases the character, but this is easily one of the most impressive and stylish. In it, Bungie reveals Bishop, a striking new Shell that immediately gives samurai robot vibes. There is no doubt this Shell will be a popular pick once it drops as part of Marathon's Symbiote update and future plans. The trailer teases some possible aspects of the Shell's kit, but we won't know its full capabilities just yet.

Bishop was previously teased as part of Marathon 's upcoming Symbiosis update , which is scheduled to launch on December 8. However, Bungie's latest cinematic offers a much better understanding of the playstyle the developer wants to encourage with the new Runner Shell. While most players would probably want to maintain some distance between themselves and their enemies in an extraction shooter, Bishop appears to thrive in close-quarters combat. Between its intimidating appearance, incredible speed, and devastating melee capabilities, the new Shell looks like something ripped straight out of a samurai fan's dreams, and that's certainly not a bad thing for Bungie's shooter.

Bungie shared the new Bishop Shell cinematic on November 24, accompanied by the tagline, "BISHOP SHELL // HUNTER KILLER. STRIKE ONCE, STRIKE FAST." Sporting a striking red chassis, an extendable blade, and leg-mounted thrusters, Bishop systematically hunts down an opposing crew throughout the trailer. The robot uses firearms alongside throwing knives, showing the diversity of its kit.

However, it's the closing moments of the cinematic that really steal the show. After being shot by an opportunistic Rook, Bishop lowers itself into a combat stance, extends its blade, and uses its thrusters to rapidly dash toward its opponent, delivering a devastating melee strike reminiscent of classic samurai films. If this is anything to go by, Bishop could be exactly the shakeup Bungie needs to keep Marathon interesting and afloat .

Mobility is king in Marathon and Bishop appears to have that in spades. It could be great at crossing open areas, and extremely deadly when fighting inside buildings or navigating narrow corridors. An aggressive Bishop player could potentially close the distance before an opponent has time to reposition, making encounters particularly unpredictable.

Of course, the cinematic isn't representative of actual gameplay, and Bungie has yet to fully detail Bishop's abilities, cooldowns, or damage output. Balancing such a mobile, melee-focused character will undoubtedly be important. Bishop is also just one reason to be excited about Marathon 's Symbiosis update. Bungie is introducing Expedition, a permanent PvE mode featuring roguelite elements, alongside an experimental 3v3 Team Deathmatch mode. Marathon's future is looking up , and Bishop is just one part of that.

What is Children of Blood and Bone about?

The first novel in the Legacy of Orïsha trilogy chronicles Zelie's journey to restore the intrinsic magic to the land after King Saran made a move to purge it, seeing it as a threat and unnatural. Drawning on African mythology, the fantasy setting contains groups of humans that practice magic known as Maji. The Maji divine certain elements, and thus are known by the specific powers they wield, from water workers beckoning tides to those like Zelie's mother Jumoke, who can summon souls.

Zelie and her brother team up with the son and daughter of King Saran. Prince Inan (Idris) has doubts about taking on his father's crown and following King Saran's example directly.

Tems serves as the soundtrack executive producer, and has contributed "African Love Song" which is featured in the film's second trailer. Beyoncé's "Energy (feat. Beam)" featured in the first trailer. Guest features on the soundtrack include:

Adeyemi co-wrote the screenplay with Prince-Bythewood. She has expressed that she won’t watch the film, and she posted a video on Instagram explaining her experience on set.

Are there more Children of Blood and Bone books? Will there be more movies?

Yes, the book gave way to a trilogy. Following Children of Blood and Bone 's publish date in 2018, Children of Virtue and Vengeance arrived in 2019, and Children of Anguish and Anarchy arrived in 2024.

There are currently no plans to adapt the next two books in the series into films.

Wu-Tang Clan has big plans for Thanksgiving. The hip-hop legends will be in Detroit to headline the halftime show for the NFL game between the host Lions and the Chicago Bears (U2 will do the halftime honors for the Thanksgiving Eve game in LA between the Green Bay Packers and the Los Angeles Rams, airing on Netflix ).

Wu-Tang, founded in Staten Island, NY, has long been considered one of the most influential groups in music history, with legions of fans worldwide and even their own acolytes known as the Killa Bees, a collective of rappers, producers, singers and others affiliated with the group. Among the most notable Bees: Cilvaringz , aka Tarik Azzougarh , a Dutch Moroccan Wu-Tang superfan turned artist whose connection to the Clan goes back to the late 1990s. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The Oscar-contending film is directed by Joanna Natasegara, the Academy Award-winning producer of The White Helmets , The Edge of Democracy , Virunga and other acclaimed documentaries. The Disciple premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January and screened in September at the Telluride Film Festival before debuting on Netflix.

DEADLINE: Have you always been into Wu-Tang? When did you learn about the story of Tarik Azzougarh?

Joanna Natasegara: I grew up in the '90s. It's exactly my era of music… Wu-Tang was just something me and my friends were very much into. We would go to clubs and listen to hip hop music, but it was something I just didn't really think about in the scope of my work, clearly for decades, actually. And so, the story [of Tarik/Cilvaringz] itself I hadn't heard of despite it being something that had gone around the world. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I was on a holiday in Morocco with my family and a script writer friend of mine came for lunch and she said, “My brother [Tarik] is having some trouble with his life story and his life rights.” And I was like, “Okay.” I knew he was Moroccan, but I thought [his story] would be something that pertained to North Africa, not to Staten Island. And she said, “Do you know the Wu-Tang?” I was like, “Yeah. I don't really know where this is going.” [She said], “He's a Killer Bee.” And I was like, “How is that possible?” And so, she told me a little part of the story, but she said, “It's so convoluted, complicated, twisty, wonderful. Can I bring him to lunch tomorrow?”

So, he came to lunch and honestly, over a three-hour lunch, he told me his whole life story. And not only did I think it was a great story, it just really resonated. We're exactly the same age. He was obviously a migrant growing up in a tiny town in Europe, and a lot of that resonated with me and he was very ambitious to make it [in the music business], and I thought that was really inspiring.

DEADLINE: It's a very complex story to tell as your feature directorial debut. About halfway into The Disciple , you really start to pivot to the sale of the kind of one-off album, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin . But as an audience we really need to understand how it all came together. We need to understand Cilvaringz, Tarik, and that's complicated. So, this is not an easy piece of storytelling to do.

JN: No, no, no, it wasn't… I wanted to build the film as a kind of homage to a Wu-Tang album. There's a lot of Easter eggs in the film — if you're a Clan fan, you can see them. But I also wanted the film to work for somebody that didn't know anything about the Wu-Tang. So that's a tricky balance to be able to tell a story that's not too complex, but also dense enough for the mega fans, and there are millions of them.

I was well held by two extremely experienced editors, Chloe Lambourne who cut for For Sama and Chris Dickens who cut for Slumdog Millionaire . And that was a lot of fun.

DEADLINE: The film does work for people who are not steeped in either hip hop or Wu-Tang or martial arts movies or “pharma bro” Martin Shkreli [who bought the one-copy only album] or other elements of the story.

JN: It's a coming-of-age story and a story about ambition because I think that's what Tarik took from RZA, what RZA took from Shifu [Shaolin monk Shi Yan Ming] and what audiences are seeming to take from Tarik. So, the album in a way is kind of a McGuffin. Obviously, some people are very attracted to know about the machinations of the album, but I'm really interested in the mentorship aspect of the film.

DEADLINE: There's the line that RZA says: “Persistence overcomes resistance,” and it's wonderful. That motto guided Tarik as a protégé of RZA and Wu-Tang, but it could also apply to you as a filmmaker.

JN: It's great, isn't it? We had t-shirts made.

DEADLINE: Towards the end of the film, you ask Tarik specifically whether producing Once Upon a Time in Shaolin was a career highlight or if it destroyed his career. And his answer is quite interesting, that he doesn't necessarily think of himself as having a career.

JN: I think he's quite honest and reflective in the piece. I thank him for that trust because that's important, isn't it, in documentary? And I think he is reflective about that process, but he's also resilient and knew what that meant to do that [album]. I think they both did, him and RZA, but the discussion [it ignited] was the point [about the value attached to a work of music] and that has worked. People are seeing that stunt and the value of music because of it. And I think it's inspired many other people to do similar things. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

The album was a perfect protest. It was a perfect way to say, why is this piece of music worth less than something that is put in an extraordinary museum? So, I think it was a really clever protest piece, and to that extent it's also worked. We're talking about it years later. So, it's a conversation that's endured and I think is really relevant not only to music now, but also to film or any piece of creative, especially as we move more and more into the dangers of AI. How much less will everything be valued, in fact?

Note: After Martin Shkreli’s conviction for fraud, the U.S. government seized his assets, including the one copy of Once Upon a Time in Shaolin encased in its custom-made box. Per a legal agreement, the album will not be available for commercial release until the year 2103. In the interim, it can only be played at limited special events.

DEADLINE: Probably the first question you get asked is, have you listened to the album?

JN: We had a beautiful listening session at Sundance, and then we had another one at Telluride. I haven't heard the whole thing. And it's probably the most frustrating thing about this film… I can't show you how good the album is; that's going to be a question for people, but it really is good… I still think all of us involved in the film or the album go back and debate, do we hope it's released? Do we not? Is it better than it isn't released? But I would really like people to be able to hear it because it’s good.

articles.title: What Happened To Harrison Ford’s Deckard After Blade Runner 2049? I Asked 2099’s EP For Her Take
articles.summary: I can't be the only one who's been wondering, right?
articles.content:
Blade Runner 2049 , in my humble opinion, is a science-fiction masterpiece. The Denis Villeneuve -directed sequel not only expertly builds upon Ridley Scott ’s 1982 film, but it also adds to the mythology in interesting ways. Additionally, the film includes a stellar performance from Harrison Ford , who reprises his role as Rick Deckard. In the near decade since the film’s release, I’ve been wondering about Deckard’s ultimate fate. So, when CinemaBlend spoke to the creator of Blade Runner 2099 , I asked for her take.

Since walking out of the theater after seeing the film for the first time in 2017, I’ve wondered about Deckard and Ana’s fates, especially with the looming war between humans and Replicants. Blade Runner 2099 creator/showrunner Silka Luisa is also a major fan of the franchise and, when she was asked for her take on what happened to Ana and Deckard, she shared some surprising comments with CB:

Considering how big a Blade Runner fan Luisa is, I’m honestly shocked over her not asking Michael Green (who shares 2049 writing credits with Hampton Fancher) for a definitive answer on Deckard and Ana. I can, however, also see Luisa’s point, though, as this franchise does leave certain plot threads open-ended, leading to fan speculation. This answer also tracks with the EP’s approach to 2099 , which is a standalone piece that doesn’t have direct references to its big-screen predecessors.

While Blade Runner ’s ending remains controversial in some circles, the discussions surrounding 2049 ’s conclusion arguably aren’t as tense. Villeneuve’s film went through different alterations during development, and even the ending changed . Fancher previously disclosed that the original plan was for Deckard to die. While that could’ve been powerful (if crafted effectively), I’m fine with Deckard not biting the big one, considering it leaves the door open for a direct sequel. And Silka Luisa is down for that as well:

For right now, though, fans can return to this dark, futuristic universe by way of 2099 . The limited series centers on dying Replicant Blade Runner Olwen (played by Michelle Yeoh ) and Cora (Hunter Schafer), a human posing as a Replicant. While fans won’t be getting answers on Deckard, the show covers plenty of ground in other respects. And, who knows, maybe we’ll actually get that 2049 sequel one day.

articles.title: Peach Momoko’s Marvel Art Book Kickstarter Pulls in a Staggering $130,000 in Just Its First Hour

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Marvel Comics is home to cavalcades of superstar, extraordinary artists, but there's nobody around like Peach Momoko . Her bold, distinct watercolor style and reimaginings of classic Marvel characters have cemented her as an artist that practically everyone wants to see work on their favorite hero, and now, fans are getting a chance to admire her wide body of work all at once. Momoko is partnering with Clover Press to bring about The Marvel Art of Peach Momoko to life. This hardcover brings her best work on Marvel's characters under one book, and fans have already shown their beyond-hearty support. The Kickstarter began with a goal of $10,000, but within the first hour, it netted over $130,000.

As of the time of writing this article, the drive has reached $500,000 and is continuing to climb, which just goes to show how much fans want to see Momoko's art tied together in a beautiful hardcover. There's much more to this book than just her art, however, as fans still have a chance to add their own contributions to get any number of additional benefits that won't be available anywhere else, even when the book releases in comic shops nationwide.

Peach Momoko has spent the last several years redefining what Marvel superheroes could look like. She made a massive name for herself with her Demon Days , which blended Marvel's heroes with Japanese folklore to create something truly unlike anything that had come before it. She'd continue to expand on her universe with Demon Wars , before becoming the main artist for Ultimate X-Men (2024), and further pumping out some of the greatest covers this side of the comic book industry. In 2024, she won her second Eisner Award for Best Cover Artist for Demon Wars: Scarlet Sin and her huge catalogue of variant covers. She was even one of the legendary artists chosen to draw a feature in Amazing Spider-Man #1000 , which goes to show just how much faith Marvel has in her appeal.

The Marvel Art of Peach Momoko is the newest entry in Clover Press's long-running The Marvel Art of… series, and they're pulling out all the stops for Momoko's collection. This 240-page hardcover brings in some of Momoko's best and most distinctive art, from her vast array of variant covers to experts from Demon Wars and Ultimate X-Men . The book itself is 9” x 12” with incredible paper quality, red-gilded edges, a spot glass cover, and a cloth bookmark. All of this is joined by 11” x 17” prints, stickers, a puzzle, signatures, and even more special delivery options that you'll need to check out for yourself on the Kickstarter.

If you wanted to mix up the cover, you'd be more than able to, as there's a wide variety of over-top covers, from a Spider-hero themed dustjacket to a Scarlet Witch and Ghost-Spider slipcase, both of which are exclusive to Kickstarter preorders. You can also pick up the Nightmare Edition, which brings in another 140 pages of Momoko's most monstrous and terrifying art, which is sure to leave you breathless from terror and awe. There's all of this and more, and with how quickly this campaign smashed its requirement, fans are sure to find everything they want and more in this collection. Here's hoping for even more incredible art from Momoko in the future .

Which character would you love to see Peach Momoko take over as the main artist for? Personally, I'd do just about anything to see her draw a few issues of the mainline Spider-Man. Let us know your choice in the comments below!

articles.title: Robert Downey Jr. Reveals How MCU Doctor Doom Will Be Different From Tony Stark in Avengers
articles.summary: With less than one month before Avengers: Doomsday finally arrives, Robert Downey Jr. has teased more about his role as Doctor Doom, including how this new villainous character is distinct from his iconic MCU role as Tony Stark/Iron Man. Over the last few days, many major Doomsday announcements have come out, including the final trailer […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google With less than one month before Avengers: Doomsday finally arrives, Robert Downey Jr. has teased more about his role as Doctor Doom, including how this new villainous character is distinct from his iconic MCU role as Tony Stark/Iron Man. Over the last few days, many major Doomsday announcements have come out, including the final trailer for the movie . Notably, and rather interestingly, that trailer really emphasized Steve Rogers' importance, with the introduction of his son, confirmation that Steve and Bucky will reunite , and seemingly proof that Steve isn't actually Loki in disguise (a very popular fan theory).

Even with so much emphasis on Steve in the most recent trailer, though, Doctor Doom remains the central figure of the movie, and audiences are going to be most curious about him, no doubt. After all, Doom has long been known to be portrayed by Robert Downey Jr., which in and of itself is mysterious, and even beyond that, so much of Doom's MCU characterization, from his backstory to his true motivations, remain unknown for now. However, ahead of the film's release, a brand-new article in Entertainment Weekly has offered Marvel fans a closer look at Doomsday , including new insight from Downey regarding his role as Doom. Check out his comments below.

About the role, Downey said, "I wanna go quadruple-meta…Let’s venture a guess and say most people know [I played Tony], then we’re really talking about shadows and reflections and symbiotic separateness. Every one of us is Tony and Victor. That’s the real big top line thing here for me. And yet, I couldn’t really reach out to Tony because I didn’t want to tread that ground. I really wanted it to feel like, even if I hadn’t ever played Stark, that Von Doom had been correctly rendered." This is particularly interesting because it seems to get at the question many fans have continued to have ahead of Doomsday : how much of a connection is there, really, between Tony and Doom?

Among the most prominent theories has been that Doom is a Tony Stark variant or vice versa. Although the Russo brothers have indicated that's not the case , that still seems like the most likely explanation for this casting choice. However, these comments from Downey do raise some questions. For one, Downey references a "symbiotic separateness," the former term of which does imply some sort of connection beyond just the fact that he has played both characters. At the same time, though, it's clear that Downey wants these to be seen as separate characters.

It's possible that this could be true and Tony and Doom could still be variants of one another, but that remains to be seen. With so much mystery surrounding the movie even now, there's certainly plenty of opportunity for Doomsday to surprise fans.

What do you think is the connection between Doctor Doom and Tony Stark, if anything? Let us know in the comments down below.

articles.summary: A prominent PlayStation 5 exclusive that was released back in 2021 is set to be shut down forever in the coming day. In the early days of the PS5, Sony released a number of games that have continued to be looked back upon fondly. Between Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales, Demon's Souls, Returnal, and Ratchet & […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A prominent PlayStation 5 exclusive that was released back in 2021 is set to be shut down forever in the coming day. In the early days of the PS5, Sony released a number of games that have continued to be looked back upon fondly. Between Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales , Demon's Souls , Returnal , and Ratchet & Clank: Rift Apart , the PS5 got off to a strong start following its arrival in late 2020. Despite this, not every game that launched in the first year of the PS5 ended up being as well-received, with one specific exclusive now slated to soon become unplayable.

As of tomorrow, November 25th, PlayStation will be shuttering the servers for Destruction AllStars . Released in February 2021, Destruction AllStars was a car combat game developed by Lucid Games. Despite being a unique concept for a live-service endeavor, Destruction AllStars failed to find an audience, which led to support for the title waning rather quickly. Now, the game's modest ongoing support is set to finally end for good when PlayStation pulls the plug on its servers in less than 24 hours.

This demise of Destruction AllStars doesn't come as a surprise, as PlayStation delisted the game suddenly on the PS Store back in May . This delisting came alongside support for the game's multiplayer functionality concluding as well. However, in the time since, single-player modes for Destruction AllStars have still been accessible, with the promise that they too would be ending on November 25th. As a result, if you have even the slightest desire to play Destruction AllStars once more before it's gone, this is your final opportunity.

While PS5 users can't be blamed for Destruction AllStars not panning out (the game wasn't very good, after all), it's still a bummer that this ended up being the title's fate. Past reports from earlier in the PS5's life cycle indicated that Lucid Games was actually in the process of working on a new entry in the Twisted Metal series before PlayStation ultimately scrapped the project. Assuming that Destruction AllStars had been a greater success, there's a world in which the game would have been a stepping stone to Twisted Metal making a comeback. Instead, the beloved PlayStation series remains dormant and will now be joined by the likes of Destruction AllStars .

How do you feel about all services and servers for Destruction AllStars coming to an end? And did you ever happen to play this PS5 exclusive game for yourself? Be sure to let me know down in the comments section.
